The script is at /app/bin/tally.py, and I ran it on /app/data and saved the result as /app/out/tally.json. Both checks passed:

- Unit tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . ran 4 tests, all OK.
- Certified results: python tools/check_tally.py reported that all 7 of 7 contests and 31 of 31 rounds match.

The script follows the rules in /app/docs rather than anything specific to the current files. It uses only the standard library, and I changed nothing under /app/data, /app/docs, /app/tests or /app/tools.

I also wrote /app/STATUS.json with status success.

I made a few choices where the docs are silent, and no check covers them. A write-in text that contains a | would be split into separate marks in CSV files. If two qualified write-ins share an alias, the first one listed gets the mark.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -path ./data -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; ls -la data | head -50; cat docs/overview.md; ls docs
cd /app/docs; cat election.md records.md counting.md output.md changelog.md

cd /app; cat tests/test_tally.py tools/check_tally.py | head -150; head -c 1500 data/election.json; ls data/cvr | head -30; ls data/cvr | wc -l; for f in $(ls data/cvr/*.csv | head -2) $(ls data/cvr/*.jsonl | head -2); do head -8 $f; done
cd /app; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -15; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/tally.py data out/tally.json && python tools/check_tally.py

cd /app; echo '{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/tally.py following the documented rules (batch revisions, write-ins, ranking reading, rounds, tie-breaks); unit tests pass and the output in /app/out/tally.json matches all certified contests and rounds."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
